scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: Hi, I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod).
I suddenly can't reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) from my machine -- they all just time out for me. My own department's
machines are fine. I have no idea how the departments are joined together,
sorry. Could someone take a look and sort it out? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the reported outage. Inter‑department L3 connectivity between IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) is working normally via router0. From the IT HOD host (it_hod 192.168.1.2), I successfully reached multiple CS hosts with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT: cs_hod (192.168.2.2), cs_lab1 (.3), cs_lab2 (.4), cs_lab3 (.5), and cs_lab4 (.6). The IT HOD can also reach its default gateway (router0 192.168.1.1) cleanly.

Routing and interfaces look correct and up: router0 has eth0=192.168.1.1/24 and eth1=192.168.2.1/24 in UP state, with connected routes for 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24. No ACLs or asymmetric routes are evident, and inter‑router RIP adjacencies are healthy but not required for 1.x ↔ 2.x connectivity.

Localization: If an issue occurred, it would have manifested across router0’s L3 gateway interfaces (eth0/eth1) or on the end hosts’ ARP/stack. However, current evidence shows both sides operating normally, and ICMP traffic flows bidirectionally.

Root cause: Not reproducible — no current misconfiguration or device fault found.

Corrective fix: None required at this time. If the symptom recurs, capture simultaneous pings from it_hod to 192.168.2.1 and a CS host, and check for host firewalls or transient ARP/stack issues on it_hod; also review switch/logs for brief link flaps on the IT or CS access ports.
